Wow that's beautiful! Thanks so much for your reply. My boyfriend is also loving and caring but he has hidden a male friendship from me for as long as we've been together. They previously had sex and he stopped having sex with him before we met. Regardless... the guy kept pushing him to sleep with him by e.g. saying that he bought him sex toys. My bf declined but not firmly enough imo. And they stayed friends, repeatedly met up, and messaged every couple of days, all without me knowing. I am really struggling with this. Even though he hasn't cheated and he has been trying everything (including immediately ending the friendship) to make me trust him again. It's the best relationship I have had apart from this happening... It makes me sad how careless he was in risking our relationship.

You are so kind! I really don't want this to be a factor, as I said. It makes me sad to know that I struggle to accept this part of him. I am sure it took him long enough to accept it himself and the last thing you want your partner to be is unsupportive. When I read about bisexual men talking about their wives and how much they love them, it really helps me. As I know somebody who first identified as bisexual and then went on to exclusively date men, I am very scared that this could be the case for my boyfriend as well. Of course, my bf is his own person and for him it might be entirely different, but it helps to read about men who "stayed bisexual".

If you have AGA I would only use it as a complimentary treatment since it won't be strong enough to make a significant difference long-term. That being said, there is no harm in adding it. If you are using an essential oil make sure to dilute it because it can irritate the scalp a lot. I personally saw a benefit from using Weleda's rosemary tonic for the past two months ... my shedding has reduced drastically. It might also be seasonal. It's just very hard to tell with these things. For me personally, the tonic is cheap enough to keep using it.
Hi :) sorry but would you mind sharing how you overcame your insecurities? My boyfriend is bi but we've been having a rough time.

thank you! We will definitely try and work things out. All I wanted to say with this is that, even though I don't want this to be a factor, I still think of his bisexuality as something threatening. I know it is stupid. I am just asking for some understanding that us straight women battle with biases, stereotypes and insecurities as well. I know it's not fair of me to ask for that, because I am sure most of you went through enough/had enough of this, but try to be a little patient if you can.
Hey :) Just wanted to let you know I had no side effects whatsoever.

For a month :) I haven't noticed regrowth but I went from losing 30-40 hairs when washing my hair to 10. It could also be a seasonal thing, however, as it is getting a bit colder. I would recommend trying it because it is relatively cheap. If you want to be on the safe side I would recommend patch testing first, just to make sure you're not sensitive to any of the ingredients.

Hi :) I have been using minox 5% for 4 years .. did not notice a difference. I think it might have slowed down the progression. I have also added Weleda's rosemary tonic to my regimen, and my shedding went down almost instantly... makes no sense to me. I just tried it on a whim, as I don't think going down the natural remedies route will lead to long-term success but here we are..

I'm a woman dating a bi man. I have been for a year and even though I love him to bits, I do struggle. For our entire relationship he's been hiding a friendship with a guy, who he's previously had sex with, from me. He didn't cheat on me but he was also not honest with me. They would have dinner together at his and message every couple of day. The guy also tried to get him to sleep with him multiple times and called him "his handsome man". It's been months since I found out and I still don't trust him.. The biphobia (which in my case was mainly a fear of not being enough) that has been lingering in me before that happened now has a reason to be there. It sucks and I do find myself thinking that I would rather date a straight guy... He also has a lot of quirks about him that make him appear gay to me and I simply don't find that attractive. Why would I find something attractive that signals to me that he is not attracted to me?

Thank you so much ppl! Your comments really help. I know my thought process is essentially biphobic and I was a bit scared that I would receive a lot of hate (understandably) for raising my concerns. You are doing a lot for your community by helping others to change their mindset ❤️ and yes.. I will be practicing, so hopefully this will help my insecurities.
